why: Civil Code article 553 (first paragraph) lets the client have the work finished by another contractor at the first contractor's cost 'under article 170'; the store jumps from article 164 to article 174, so the conditions of that alternative to rescission could not be read.

When the defendant is a professional seller or service provider, the consumer-protection law (guarantee, conformity) may give the buyer remedies that overlap rescission; the law is not in the store. The article number is from memory and may be wrong: the whole guarantee chapter is wanted.

CPCA article 17 (third paragraph) requires the petition about a published real right to be published at the land registry; the decree on the land register sets how the petition is published. Not in the store; the article number is from memory.

Whether a sale or works contract is commercial decides the section (CPCA 531), the free proof of commercial contracts (Commercial Code 30), the territorial options of CPCA 39 (fifth paragraph) and the validity of a jurisdiction clause (CPCA 45). The store holds the Commercial Code only from article 30; articles 1 to 4 (commercial acts) are wanted.

For the rescission of a sale of real property: when ownership passed (publication) decides what restitution covers and why the petition must be published. Not in the store; the article number is from memory.
